implementation_record.ac_166_2_form: Helper function fn::mt166_resource_select_grant($resource: record<protected_resources>) called from the select PERMISSIONS as fn::mt166_resource_select_grant(id). A PERMISSIONS clause cannot declare LET, and $parent.id / $auth.* are Param-rooted idioms the 3.2.0 exec planner does not fold (exec/planner/util/params.rs replaces only bare Expr::Param). UDF arguments are bound with with_param (exec/physical_expr/function/user_defined.rs:41-55) and the helper LET-binds $auth.account_id/principal_id/access_space_id, so all four resource_grants_exact_idx columns compare to literals. The helper inherits skip_fetch_perms in the predicate context (user_defined.rs:83), so its SELECT runs perms-off exactly like the old inline subquery. Choice: a helper fn (not reusing an existing fn) because no existing function has these exact six conditions.
condition_mapping_protected_resources_se: grant subquery resource_id = $parent.id -> helper resource_id = $resource (called with id, the same record)
(expires_at = NONE OR expires_at > time::now()) -> helper identical
condition_mapping_ledger_access: actions CONTAINS $action AND capability_ids CONTAINS $capability -> grant WHERE identical

(resource_id.resource_kind != 'reconciliation_queue' OR (principal_id.principal_kind = 'service_identity' AND principal_id.capability_profile_id = 'MT109Reconciler')) -> LET $not_reconciliation = $resource.resource_kind != 'reconciliation_queue'; grant WHERE ($not_reconciliation OR (identical principal clause))
implementation_record.equivalence_note: Moving resource_id.* checks out of the grant WHERE is exact because every candidate row has resource_id = $resource, so each check reads the same record; a dangling $resource gives NONE and false in both forms. Early exits are pure reads with no side effects.
